name: Zendrop
summary: AI dropshipping and print-on-demand for Shopify: browse 1M+ products from US and global suppliers, link them to your store and let fulfilment and tracking run automatically, with custom branding, POD and 3PL as you scale.
best_for: Shopify merchants starting or scaling a dropshipping or print-on-demand store who want sourcing, automated fulfilment, tracking and custom branding in one app, and who can price the per-order product and shipping cost into their margins
skip_if: you already have supplier relationships worth keeping, or you need the cheapest possible international shipping: the vetted US supplier network is the selling point here and you pay for it
honest_knock: The free plan is a catalogue browser rather than a working tier: it allows no linked products, so nothing can actually be sold through it. Past that you are paying for an allowance, not for capability: Beginner, Pro and Plus carry exactly the same feature list, and the only thing $79 buys over $29 is room for more than a hundred linked products. The subscription is also the smaller half of the bill: product and shipping cost lands per order on top, and Zendrop bills that separately from your Shopify invoice, so the figure you budget is not the figure you pay. Their own pricing page and the App Store listing do not agree: the site sells Free, Pro and Plus with annual rates and no $29 tier, which means the price depends on where you sign up. And the 4.5 average covers a split verdict, with 83% five stars alongside 7% one star across 1,264 reviews (read 5 October 2026): 86 people rating it bottom of the scale. In our own test of 17 November 2026 the app's onboarding offered only Plus and a Flex route, so the listing's $29 and $49 tiers and its free level were not on offer inside the app.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/zendrop and in our own test that day; earlier: re-read 2026-09-18 and again on 2026-10-05 on apps.shopify.com/zendrop and on zendrop.com/pricing — the two do not carry the same ladder) On the Shopify listing: free to install, with three paid tiers, Beginner $29, Pro $49 and Plus $79 a month. What separates them is not features but how many products you may link to your store. The free tier allows none at all (“No linked products allowed”), Beginner covers 1-20, Pro 21-100 and Plus 101 or more; the feature list on all three paid tiers is identical (trending products, Zendrop Academy, Zendrop AI access, custom branding). Product and shipping cost is charged per order on top of every plan, and the listing states that external charges may be billed by Zendrop separately from your Shopify invoice. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.5 from 1,264 App Store reviews on 5 October 2026, after 4.6 from 1,258 on 18 September and 4.5 from 1,191 on 19 August; the spread is 83% five-star (1.0K), 7% four-star (94), 1% three-star (18), 1% two-star (18) and 7% one-star (86). The listing does not carry Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. Developer Zendrop, 5499 North Federal Highway, Suite R, Boca Raton, FL, 33487, US; the app launched 4 November 2020. On zendrop.com/pricing the ladder is different: Free $0, Pro $49 a month or $399 a year, and Plus $79 a month or $549 a year, marked Most Popular. There is no $29 Beginner tier on their own site, and the annual rates appear only there — $399 is $33.25 a month and $549 is $45.75. The Summer Promo recorded here on 19 August 2026 (65% off annual Plus for the first year, advertised as a $357 saving, plus $100 in order credits, ending 31 August 2026) is gone: the page carries no percentage-off offer at all on 18 September or 5 October 2026. Their own site also lists products the App Store listing does not mention, including AI-Built Stores, an AI Ad Generator and an MCP Server for connecting AI agents to a store. Read again on 17 November 2026: the listing is unchanged, free to install with no linked products allowed, Beginner $29, Pro $49 and Plus $79 a month, and shows 4.5 from 1,300 reviews. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store the app's onboarding did not show that ladder. It offered two ways to activate: Plus, “7 days free, then $79/mo”, with a one off upsell at $197 a year that the same screen marked down from $549, and Flex, pay as you go, for which Shopify's approval screen showed a usage subscription with an app spending limit of $79.00 per 30 days and an Add payment method row. We saw no Beginner or Pro plan and no free level inside the app, and we could not reach the product catalogue without choosing one of the two. The $197 offer is a temporary promotion on the app's screen and not on the listing, so we do not count it as the price. We did not approve anything.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session installed Zendrop on a Shopify development store. After a Black Friday offer the onboarding showed only Plus and Flex, both with a payment step and no route to the catalogue, and the Shopify approval screen for Flex asked for a payment method, so the catalogue was not tested. The app was uninstalled; nothing was paid and no Zendrop account was made. Install: the install started at about 23:26; the dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and Install was clicked. The app sent us straight to the Zendrop onboarding without a login screen or account question. The first screen was a Black Friday offer: 64% Off Zendrop Plus, Plus $197 /year, Regularly priced at $549, a 5-day money-back guarantee and No thanks, I'll skip this offer, which was clicked. Core action NOT DONE: the next screen, Finish your setup to start selling, offers only two ways to activate Zendrop, both with a payment step, and gives no route to the product catalogue without one of them. No product was searched or imported and no sample or order was placed. Plans in the onboarding: Plus (Unlimited Access), Start Free Trial, 7 days free, then $79/mo, Cancel anytime, with a list of extras such as order credits, coaching and print on demand; and Flex, Pay as you go, Add a payment method in Shopify and approve Zendrop, Continue to Shopify, Free to start, Cancel anytime. Checkout: Flex opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription for Zendrop - Dropshipping & POD: This app bills you for usage charges, plan Based usage, an app spending limit of at most $79,00 USD per 30 days, You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it, a greyed out Approve and the row Add payment method. The line You will not be billed for this test charge was NOT on the screen, so nothing was approved. The Plus trial was not clicked. Difference with the dossier: the dossier names Beginner $29/mo, Pro $49/mo and a free level without linked products; the listing still shows them, but the onboarding showed only Plus and Flex. Cancelling: never approved, so nothing to cancel. The uninstall dialog needs a reason and says a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information; Zendrop was uninstalled. Clean up: no theme change, no products and no orders. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The onboarding opens on a yearly Black Friday upsell, then offers only Plus or a usage plan, both with a payment step; the cheaper plans and the free level on the listing were not offered.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?

Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?

vendor_mcp.what: Server for their dropshipping platform: search the catalog, request shipping methods and delivery windows per country, list and filter orders with tracking, pull revenue, profit and refund analytics, and trigger fulfilment behind a built-in confirmation step. Access runs on a token you generate, can scope to read-only and can revoke.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their FAQ answers it directly: "Do I need a paid Zendrop plan to use the MCP server? You can get started free. Some features may require a paid plan depending on your store's volume and needs." No tier is named.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
